revisions.invariant: Proved unassisted that TCP vs UDP enforces deterministic causal ordering and bounded blast radius by strictly decoupling volatile state from the critical write path.
revisions.failureBoundary: Under 1-2% loss on high BDP links (>50ms RTT), Mathis formula throughput collapses (Throughput <= (MSS / RTT) * (1 / sqrt(p))).
revisions.formula: Throughput <= (MSS / RTT) * (1 / sqrt(p)) [Mathis Equation] | BDP = RTT × Bandwidth
revisions.defenseAnswer: Learner evaluated physical failure modes and quantitative boundaries during self evaluation.
revisions.realityCheckPrompt: Under 1% network packet loss on a 50ms link, why does an HTTP/2 connection stall across all multiplexed streams, and why does VoD use TCP while live videoconferencing picks UDP?
guarantees: Verified operational ordering, bounded blast radius, and deterministic recovery.
taxes: Coordination overhead, queueing jitter under packet loss, and protocol complexity.
revisions.ruleOfThumb: Use single-stream TCP when sequential byte-stream order is strictly mandatory. Switch to QUIC/multiplexed UDP when concurrent independent requests share a lossy link.
revisions.naiveTrap: Assumed critical RPCs should universally mandate TCP for reliability, treating packet loss purely as a transport concern transparent to application latency.

revisions.invariant: QUIC shifts reliable transport and crypto handshakes from kernel OS space into user-space UDP datagrams, isolating packet loss to individual stream frames.
revisions.failureBoundary: NAT rebinding during cellular-to-Wi-Fi handoff breaks 4-tuple TCP connections; QUIC connection ID (CID) enables seamless migration without reconnecting.
revisions.formula: Handshake RTT: 0-RTT (resumed) or 1-RTT (initial) vs TCP+TLS 1.3 (2-3 RTT)
revisions.defenseAnswer: QUIC packets carry independent stream IDs. Dropping a packet for stream #3 halts decoding for stream #3 only; streams #1 and #2 continue reading immediately.
revisions.realityCheckPrompt: How does QUIC maintain connection continuity across IP address changes without renegotiating TLS?
guarantees: Cryptographic connection migration across cellular/Wi-Fi handoffs
taxes: Higher userspace CPU utilization (UDP syscall overhead)
Middlebox UDP rate limiting and packet drop policies
revisions.ruleOfThumb: Deploy HTTP/2 on high-reliability internal server-to-server backbones; deploy HTTP/3/QUIC on public internet edge and lossy mobile client networks.
revisions.naiveTrap: Assuming HTTP/2 multiplexing is unconditionally faster than HTTP/1.1 on lossy wireless networks.

revisions.topicTitle: LSM Trees: MemTable, SSTables, and Leveled Compaction
revisions.invariant: LSM engines trade read latency and compaction write amplification for sequential disk write throughput via append-only commit logs and sorted string tables.
revisions.failureBoundary: Write stalls occur when background compaction threads cannot keep pace with write ingestion, forcing write rate throttling to avoid SSTable unbounded accumulation.
revisions.formula: Write Amplification Factor (WAF) = Total Bytes Written to Disk / Bytes Ingested (typically 10-30x in leveled compaction)
revisions.defenseAnswer: LSM writes strictly append to an in-memory MemTable and on-disk WAL. Reads must check MemTable, Bloom filters, and multi-level SSTables, demanding Bloom filter cache tuning.
revisions.realityCheckPrompt: Why does an LSM engine trigger write stalls even when spare disk storage is plentiful?
guarantees: Sequential disk writes for high ingest throughput
Immutable SSTables simplify crash recovery and concurrency
taxes: High background write amplification and disk wear
Read amplification mitigated only by Bloom filters
revisions.ruleOfThumb: Use LSM-Trees for high-velocity write ingest (logs, metrics, timeseries); use B-Trees for read-heavy workloads with complex range filters and covering index requirements.
revisions.naiveTrap: Assuming LSM disk append speed means compaction comes with zero background I/O performance tax.

revisions.topicTitle: Raft Leader Election, Log Replication & Quorums
revisions.invariant: Raft guarantees strong state machine safety across asymmetric network partitions through strict term monotonicity and majoritarian log matching: a leader must possess all committed entries from prior terms.
revisions.failureBoundary: In an asymmetric network partition where a leader can talk to clients but not to a majority of followers, reads without lease verification return stale uncommitted data.
revisions.formula: Quorum Size Q = floor(N / 2) + 1 (Fault tolerance F = floor((N - 1) / 2))
revisions.defenseAnswer: Raft avoids split-brain by requiring strict majority quorum (N/2 + 1) for both leader election and entry commitment. Two majorities in a cluster of size N must intersect by at least one common node.
revisions.realityCheckPrompt: Explain how Raft prevents two leaders from committing divergent entries in the same term.
guarantees: Deterministic automatic failover within randomized election timeout
taxes: Minimum 3 nodes required to tolerate 1 failure; 5 nodes for 2 failures
Write latency bounded by slowest node in the majority quorum
revisions.ruleOfThumb: Always deploy odd cluster sizes (3, 5, 7) for consensus. Implement leader leases and generation term counters before serving linearizable reads.
revisions.naiveTrap: Assuming adding an even node (e.g. 4th node to a 3-node cluster) increases fault tolerance; it actually reduces availability under network partitions.

revisions.failureBoundary: HoL blocking in HTTP/2 stalls every request on the connection when 1 packet drops. HTTP/1.1 bounds the stall to 1 of 6 connections.

revisions.realityCheckPrompt: In a hospital on-call database where at least one doctor must be active, two doctors simultaneously attempt to go off call under Snapshot Isolation. Both read 2 active doctors. Why does Snapshot Isolation permit both (Write Skew), and what pattern prevents it?
revisions.invariant: Snapshot Isolation prevents dirty reads and non-repeatable reads by checking write-write conflicts on identical rows, but CANNOT detect cross-row constraint violations where concurrent transactions read overlapping rows and write to disjoint rows (Write Skew).
revisions.failureBoundary: Both doctors successfully go off call, violating the invariant of having at least one active doctor, with zero transaction errors or deadlocks.
revisions.formula: Serializable Isolation or explicit SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (pessimistic locking) is mathematically mandatory to eliminate Write Skew.
revisions.ruleOfThumb: When a business decision reads across multiple rows to validate a constraint before writing, standard Snapshot Isolation is insufficient: enforce Serializable or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.
revisions.naiveTrap: Believing that 'running inside a database transaction' automatically prevents all concurrency bugs and data anomalies.
revisions.defenseAnswer: Write skew occurs because neither transaction modifies a row that the other modified; they read overlapping state and write to separate rows, bypassing first-committer-wins row locks.
guarantees: Consistent snapshot reads without blocking concurrent writers
taxes: Vulnerability to phantom reads and write skew without explicit locks
